payload.question: What sustains an institutions existence over time in this ontology?
payload.answer: According to this ontology, an institution's existence over time is sustained by several interrelated mechanisms: (1) Recognition — specifically ongoing, collective, and recursive recognition processes (OngoingRecognitionProcess, RecognitionSustainingProcess, RecursiveReinforcement, ContinualRecognitionProcess) that continuously maintain the institutional entity; (2) InstitutionalSustainment — a disposition/process that keeps the institution in existence; (3) ParticipantIndependentPersistence — the institution persists even as individual participants change (ParticipantTurnover, PersonnelTurnover); (4) RecognitionStabilization and RelationalSustainment — stable patterns of recognition relations among agents ground institutional continuity; (5) InstitutionalPersistence as a quality (a BFO quality) inherent to institutions; (6) CollectiveMaintenance — agents collectively upholding the institution through practices (CollectiveUpholdingProcess, SustainingPractice); (7) InstitutionalMemory and OntologicalMemory — dispositions that carry forward recognition effects across time; (8) EnduringInstitutionalForm and EnduringInstitutionalReality — the enduring structural forms that persist through time; and (9) SustainingJudgment and SustainingHabit — dispositions of officials that maintain the recognition structure. The ontology treats institutional existence as recognition-dependent: without ongoing collective recognition, institutions cease to exist.
